name: Bagalkot
monumentDescription: Four 6th–8th century rock-cut sandstone sanctuaries excavated into red cliffs overlooking Agastya Lake, featuring Cave 3's dated 578 CE inscription of Mangalesha.
culturalSignificance: Crucible of Early Chalukyan temple architecture bridging Nagara and Dravida styles alongside nearby Pattadakal (UNESCO Ref. 239) and Aihole.
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & UNESCO World Heritage Centre
description: Home to the Malaprabha River basin sites of Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal, representing the formative crucible of Early Chalukyan temple architecture alongside living Ilkal handloom weaving.
history: Badami (ancient Vatapi) served as the royal capital of the Early Chalukyas from the 6th to 8th centuries CE under rulers including Pulakeshin I, Mangalesha, and Pulakeshin II. Cave 3 preserves an inscribed record dated 578 CE, while nearby Pattadakal hosted royal coronations and Aihole functioned as an experimental guild center for Deccan temple architecture.
arts: Early Chalukyan Rock-Cut & Structural Stone Sculpture
Ilkal Handloom Saree Weaving (GI App. No. 76, 2007)
traditions: Tope-tenni Interlocking Loom Joinery in Ilkal
Malaprabha Basin Agastya Tank & Mahakuta Pilgrimage
heritageSites: Badami Rock-Cut Cave Temples & Bhutanatha Group
Group of Monuments at Pattadakal (UNESCO Ref. 239, 1987)

name: Ballari
geoBoundaryNote: In the 2021 geoBoundaries LGD boundary layer, this polygon encompasses both Ballari and Vijayanagara (carved out in November 2021).
monumentDescription: Two-tiered granite hill fortress rising atop Bellary Gudda, constructed under Hanumappa Nayaka during the Vijayanagara era and reinforced in stone under Hyder Ali in the 18th century.
culturalSignificance: Marks the eastern Deccan frontier linking Vijayanagara-period hill defense architecture, Sandur Lambani needlecraft (GI No. 132), and Bayalata folk theatre.
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Protected Monument
description: Eastern Deccan plateau district anchored by the granite citadel of Ballari Fort, Sandur's GI-tagged Lambani embroidery cooperatives, and rural Bayalata folk theatre.
history: Historically linked with the Vijayanagara frontier and later administered by Hande Hanumappa Nayaka, Hyder Ali, and British Deccan garrisons, Ballari also nurtured Sandur's princely craft guilds. On November 17, 2021, western taluks including Hampi were separated to form Vijayanagara district.
cuisine: Jolada Rotti with Brinjal & Groundnut Chutneys
traditions: Sandur Kala Kendra Women's Mirror-Work Guilds
Granite Hilltop Fortification & Rainwater Cistern Stewardship

Ballari District Official Heritage & History Portal

name: Belagavi
monumentDescription: 13th-century stone fortress initiated by the Ratta dynasty of Saundatti, enclosing the carved Chalukyan-style Kamala Basadi Jain shrine (1204 CE) and Adil Shahi bastions.
culturalSignificance: Illustrates layered Deccan heritage where Ratta Jain temple carving coexists with Kittur Rani Chennamma's 1824 anti-colonial citadel and Belagavi Kunda confectionery.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Sahyadri borderland district centered on Ratta-era Belagavi Fort, Kittur Rani Chennamma's historic citadel, Gokak handlooms, and famed caramelized Belagavi Kunda.
history: Historically known as Venugrama, Belagavi flourished under the Ratta rulers who built Kamala Basadi in 1204 CE before passing through Vijayanagara, Adil Shahi, and Maratha hands. In 1824 CE, Rani Chennamma of Kittur led one of India's earliest armed uprisings against the British East India Company from nearby Kittur Fort.
arts: Gokak Lacquered Wooden Toys & Carved Fruits
Lavani & Gee Gee Pada Folk Ballads
traditions: Rani Chennamma Heroic Ballads & Oral Commemoration
Sahyadri Borderland Handloom & Dairy Sweet Guilds
heritageSites: Kittur Rani Chennamma Fort & Archaeological Museum

sources.organization: District Administration Belagavi, Government of Karnataka

name: Bengaluru Rural
monumentDescription: Oval granite bastion fortress built around 1501 CE by Malla Byregowda of the Avati Nadaprabhu chieftains and later rebuilt in dressed stone under Hyder Ali.
culturalSignificance: Preserves 16th-century circular granite fortification architecture, historic Venugopalaswamy temple carvings, and Shivagange's monolithic pilgrimage hill.
description: Highland agrarian district surrounding the capital, anchored by 1501 CE Devanahalli Fort, Nelamangala's Shivagange hill sanctuary, and Doddaballapura silk weaving.
history: Devanahalli emerged under Avati chieftain Malla Byregowda in 1501 CE before becoming an important Mysore garrison in the 18th century and the birthplace of Tipu Sultan. Nelamangala and Doddaballapura also preserve Chola-Vijayanagara inscriptions and long-standing powerloom and handloom silk weaving clusters.
cuisine: Ragi Mudde with Avarekalu Saaru (Hyacinth Bean Curry)
traditions: Avarekalu Winter Harvest Gatherings
Kalyani & Village Irrigation Tank Maintenance

name: Bengaluru Urban
monumentDescription: Two-storey Indo-Islamic pavilion completed in 1791 CE using carved teakwood pillars, cusped arches, and floral frescoes adjacent to Kempegowda's Bangalore Fort.
culturalSignificance: Rare surviving 18th-century timber-framed court residence beside the 1537 CE Kempegowda urban core, Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, and the century-old Bengaluru Karaga festival.
description: Capital district of Karnataka uniting Kempegowda-era urban tanks and pete markets with Tipu Sultan's teakwood pavilion, Bangalore Palace, and the historic Bengaluru Karaga festival.
history: Founded in 1537 CE by Kempe Gowda I with fortified pete quarters, watchtowers, and interconnected rainwater tanks, Bengaluru later evolved under Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan, and the Wadiyar administration into a major center of Carnatic music sabhas, botanical gardens (Lalbagh), and civic architecture.
festivals: Bengaluru Karaga (Dharmaraya Swamy Temple, Chaitra Full Moon)
Lalbagh Independence & Republic Day Flower Shows
cuisine: Bisi Bele Bath & Chow Chow Bath
Bengaluru Masala Dosa & Darshini Filter Coffee
traditions: Annual Midnight Karaga Procession Across Old Pete
Traditional Basavanagudi Farmer Harvest Fair (Kadalekai Parishe)
heritageSites: Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi) & Gavigangadhareshwara Cave Temple

sources.title: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace ASI Record

name: Bidar
monumentDescription: 15th-century Bahmani Sultanate citadel built along the edge of a red laterite plateau, featuring triple moats, glazed Persian tilework in Rangeen Mahal, and subterranean karez channels.
culturalSignificance: Center of Deccan Indo-Persian architecture, historic karez water engineering, Basavakalyan Vachana heritage, and GI-certified Bidriware silver-inlay metalcraft (GI No. 21).
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & World Monuments Fund
description: Northernmost laterite plateau district famed for Bahmani fort architecture, Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, historic karez subterranean aqueducts, Basavakalyan's 12th-century Anubhava Mantapa tradition, and GI-certified Bidriware.
history: Bidar rose as the second capital of the Bahmani Sultanate under Ahmad Shah Wali in the 1420s and later the Barid Shahi kingdom, attracting Persian scholars and artisans. Earlier, Basavakalyan (Kalyana) in Bidar district was the 12th-century seat of the Kalyana Chalukyas and the epicenter of Basavanna's Vachana social-literary movement.
traditions: Tarkashi Silver Inlay & Bidar Fort Soil Oxidation
Karez Subterranean Spring Aqueduct Heritage
heritageSites: Basavakalyan Fort & Anubhava Mantapa Heritage Zone

name: Chamarajanagar
monumentDescription: Cliff-top Dravidian shrine perched at roughly 1,550 meters elevation where the Western and Eastern Ghats converge, revered across Soliga indigenous and regional communities.
culturalSignificance: Embodies biocultural coexistence within the BRT forested landscape alongside Male Mahadeshwara Hills, Himavad Gopalaswamy Betta, and Beesu Kamsale devotional music.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Endowments & Forest Heritage Documentation
description: Southernmost ecological and cultural corridor where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet, famed for Soliga forest traditions, Male Mahadeshwara Hills, and Beesu Kamsale folk performance.
history: Named after Chamaraja Wadiyar IX, the district spans ancient Chola, Hoysala, and Wadiyar inscriptions alongside the ancestral forest territories of the Soliga people. Its hilltop shrines at Male Mahadeshwara Betta and Biligirirangana Betta gave rise to vibrant oral epics sung with bronze kamsale cymbals.
festivals: Male Mahadeshwara Hills Deepavali & Maha Shivaratri Jatra
arts: Soliga Oral Forest Songs & Bamboo Craft
cuisine: Ragi Mudde with Forest Greens (Soppu Saaru)
traditions: Soliga Community Forest & Wildlife Co-stewardship
Kamsale Oral Epics of Madeshwara (Manteswamy & Male Mahadeshwara)

name: Chikkaballapura
monumentLocation: Nandi Village, Foothills of Nandi Hills
monumentDescription: Granite temple complex founded under Bana and Nolamba patronage in the 9th century CE and expanded by Chola, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara dynasties with a carved stepped kalyani tank.
culturalSignificance: Architectural palimpsest of five southern Indian dynasties beneath Nandi Durga hill fort, linked also with Sir M. Visvesvaraya's birthplace at Muddenahalli.
description: Granite hill district at the headwaters of the Arkavathi and Palar rivers, distinguished by the 9th-century Bhoga Nandeeshwara temple complex, Nandidurga fort, and Gudibande's stepped fort.
history: Situated beneath Nandi Durga hill fort, Nandi village preserves continuous epigraphic strata spanning Bana, Nolamba, Chola, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara dynasties. Muddenahalli in this district is the birthplace of engineer-statesman Bharat Ratna Sir M. Visvesvaraya.
festivals: Maha Shivaratri & Rathotsava at Bhoga Nandeeshwara
traditions: Stepped Shringi Tirtha Kalyani Ritual Bathing
Sir M. Visvesvaraya Memorial Engineering Heritage
heritageSites: Sir M. Visvesvaraya Memorial Museum, Muddenahalli

name: Chikkamagaluru
monumentDescription: 1196 CE Hoysala soapstone shrine commissioned by general Amriteshwara Dandanayaka, famed for its scalloped mantapa ceilings and epic narrative reliefs.
culturalSignificance: Showcases mature Hoysala chloritic schist artistry nestled in the Malnad foothills alongside Sringeri Sharada Peetham, Belavadi, and Baba Budangiri's coffee heritage.
description: Western Ghats coffee and temple highland spanning Sringeri's 14th-century Vidyashankara temple, Amruthapura, Belavadi, and the Baba Budangiri range where Indian coffee cultivation began.
history: Chikkamagaluru includes Angadi (ancient Sosevur), remembered in Hoysala inscriptions as the dynasty's ancestral home, and Sringeri Sharada Peetham established by Adi Shankaracharya on the banks of the Tunga River. In the 17th century, Sufi saint Baba Budan introduced coffee beans to the Chandradrona hills.
cuisine: Pathrode (Colocasia Leaf Rolls) & Bamboo Shoot Curry
traditions: Sringeri Vedic & Sanskrit Manuscript Preservation
Antike-Pantike Monsoon & Deepavali Folk Singing

name: Chitradurga
monumentDescription: Seven-ringed granite boulder fortress engineered by the Madakari Nayaka dynasty between the 14th and 18th centuries with interconnected rainwater reservoirs and 19 gateways.
culturalSignificance: Masterpiece of Deccan military hydrology and Karnataka's hero-lore remembering Onake Obavva and Madakari Nayaka V alongside prehistoric Chandravalli.
description: Central Deccan fort-town dominated by the seven concentric stone ramparts of Chitradurga Fort, Chandravalli's Satavahana-era caves, and Ashokan rock edicts at Brahmagiri.
history: Chitradurga preserves continuous human history from Megalithic and Satavahana settlements at Chandravalli and Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts at Brahmagiri (Molakalmuru) to the Nayaka chieftains. Under Madakari Nayaka V, the hill citadel endured Hyder Ali's sieges, immortalizing the courage of Onake Obavva.
arts: Molakalmuru Pure Silk Handloom Sarees (GI App. No. 53, 2007)
cuisine: Jolada Rotti & Ragi Mudde (Transitional Deccan Cuisine)
traditions: Onake Obavva Heroic Oral Memory at Kindi Gate
Interconnected Granite Tank Rainwater Harvesting

name: Dakshina Kannada
monumentDescription: Coastal shrine complex housing a dated 968 CE Alupa bronze Lokeshwara image, laterite-tiled coastal roofs, and nine stepped spring tanks.
culturalSignificance: Reflects coastal Tuluva syncretic heritage linking Natha traditions, Moodabidri Jain basadis, Tenkuthittu Yakshagana, Bhoota Kola, and seasonal Kambala.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology & KSTDC
description: Coastal Tuluva region renowned for Tenkuthittu Yakshagana theatre, seasonal Kambala buffalo-race traditions, Bhoota Kola spirit worship, and Moodabidri's Jain basadis.
history: Ruled for centuries by the coastal Alupa dynasty and local Chauta and Banga chiefs, Dakshina Kannada prospered through Arabian Sea spice trade from Mangaluru. It preserved rich Tuluva oral epics (Paddanas), palm-leaf Jain manuscripts at Moodabidri, and coastal laterite temple architecture.
festivals: Nema / Bhoota Kola Annual Village Rituals
arts: Tulu Paddana Epic Singing & Bhoota Brass Casting
traditions: Bhoota Aradhane (Daivaradhane) Ancestral Village Covenant
Aliyasantana Matrilineal Kinship Traditions

Saavira Kambada Basadi (Thousand Pillar Temple), Moodabidri

name: Davanagere
monumentDescription: Monumental 16th-century stepped stone water tank centered around an octagonal Vasant Mantapa pavilion built by Nayaka chieftain Kenga Hanumappa.
culturalSignificance: Celebrated example of post-Vijayanagara hydraulic architecture alongside the 1223 CE Hoysala Harihareshwara Temple on the Tungabhadra river.
description: Central Karnataka plains district uniting the Santhebennur Pushkarani, Hoysala-era Harihareshwara Temple, Sulekere (Shanti Sagara) medieval tank, and iconic Benne Dose cuisine.
history: Located along the Tungabhadra corridor, Davanagere preserves 11th-century Chalukyan and 13th-century Hoysala temples at Bagali and Harihar, the monumental 12th-century Shanti Sagara (Sulekere) irrigation reservoir, and Nayaka-period hydraulic heritage at Santhebennur.
arts: Chalukyan & Hoysala Stone Relief Craft (Bagali & Harihar)
cuisine: Davanagere Benne Dose (Crisp Butter Dosa & Potato Palya)
traditions: Shanti Sagara (Sulekere) Historic Tank Irrigation Stewardship
Davanagere Commercial & Cotton-Town Merchant Traditions

name: Dharwad
monumentDescription: 12th-century Kalyana Chalukyan cruciform stone temple distinguished by four ornate cardinal entrances, dual Nandi shrines, and pierced stone latticework.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Dharwad's Chalukyan heritage alongside Hindustani music gharanas (Gangubai Hangal, Mallikarjun Mansur, Bhimsen Joshi), Kasuti embroidery, and GI-tagged Dharwad Peda.
description: Cultural and literary capital of northern Karnataka, celebrated for Hindustani classical music maestros, Kasuti embroidery, Kalyana Chalukya shrines, and GI-certified Dharwad Peda.
history: From medieval Kalyana Chalukyan temples at Unkal, Annigeri, and Kundgol to 19th–20th century literary renaissance led by Karnataka Vidyavardhaka Sangha, Dharwad became a national cradle of Hindustani classical vocalists—nurturing legends such as Sawai Gandharva, Mallikarjun Mansur, Gangubai Hangal, and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi.
festivals: Dharwad Utsav & Sawai Gandharva Music Traditions
arts: Dharwad Kasuti Hand Embroidery (GI App. No. 55, 2007)
Navalgund Durries (Cotton Rug Weaving, GI App. No. 131)
traditions: Gurukul Hindustani Music Sabha Traditions
Karnataka Vidyavardhaka Sangha Literary Heritage (Est. 1890)
heritageSites: Gangubai Hangal Music Gurukul & Memorial, Hubballi

name: Gadag
monumentDescription: 11th-century Kalyana Chalukya soapstone masterwork celebrated for deeply undercut stone toranas, twin shrines, and nearby stepwells (kalyanis) across Lakkundi.
culturalSignificance: Crucial stylistic bridge between Early Chalukyan stone carving and ornate Hoysala sculpture, accompanied by Trikuteshwara Temple in Gadag and Hindustani maestro Puttaraj Gawai's Veereshwara Punyashrama.
description: Home to the Kalyana Chalukya temple clusters of Lakkundi, Dambal, and Gadag, alongside the famed Veereshwara Punyashrama music school and Ron handloom weaving.
history: Lakkundi (ancient Lokkigundi) served as a prominent royal mint and architectural center of the Kalyana Chalukyas in the 10th–12th centuries CE, home to patron Attimabbe and master architect Jakanachari's stylistic predecessors. In the 20th century, Pandit Puttaraj Gawai established Gadag's inclusive music academy for visually impaired musicians.
traditions: 101 Temples & 101 Stepwells Preservation of Lakkundi
Inclusive Gurukul Music Education at Veereshwara Punyashrama
heritageSites: Kasivisvesvara Temple & Muskin Bhavi Stepwell, Lakkundi

name: Hassan
monumentDescription: 12th-century UNESCO-inscribed Hoysala chloritic schist sanctuary built in 1117 CE on a stellate plinth with lathe-turned pillars and signed sculptures.
culturalSignificance: Heartland of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (UNESCO Ref. 1670) alongside Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu and Shravanabelagola's 10th-century Gommateshwara monolith.
description: Heartland of the Hoysala Empire and ancient Jain heritage, housing the UNESCO-inscribed sanctuaries of Belur and Halebidu alongside Shravanabelagola.
history: Initiated in 1117 CE under King Vishnuvardhana at Belur and expanded at Dorasamudra (Halebidu), Hoysala temple workshops created signed soapstone sculptures on star-shaped plinths. Earlier, in 981 CE, Western Ganga minister Chavundaraya commissioned the 17.5-meter monolithic Bahubali statue at Vindhyagiri Hill, Shravanabelagola.
arts: Hoysala Chloritic Schist Carving & Madanika Bracket Figures
cuisine: Akki Rotti, Halu Bai & Malnad-Maidan Kadubu
traditions: Signed Medieval Guild Sculptor Inscriptions
Twelve-Year Jain Anointment Rituals at Vindhyagiri
heritageSites: Buchesvara Temple, Koravangala & Lakshmi Devi Temple, Doddagaddavalli

name: Haveri
monumentDescription: 11th-century Kalyana Chalukyan sandstone temple marked by a distinctive pyramidal stepped shikhara towering along the Tungabhadra–Varada river confluence.
culturalSignificance: Celebrated for Chalukyan temple craft at Galaganatha, Haveri, and Hangal, alongside Kanakadasa's bhakti poetry at Kaginele and Shishunala Sharif's syncretic tatvapada songs.
description: Tungabhadra–Varada riverine district rich in Chalukyan temples, Kaginele Haridasa heritage of Kanakadasa, Shishunala Sharif's syncretic mysticism, and Byadgi chilli traditions.
history: Flourishing under the Kadambas of Hangal and Kalyana Chalukyas, Haveri later became the spiritual heart of 16th-century Haridasa poet-saint Kanakadasa at Kaginele and 19th-century mystic poet Shishunala Sharif, whose Kannada tatvapada songs remain central to Karnataka folk music.
festivals: Shishunala Sharif & Guru Govinda Bhatta Commemoration
arts: Kalyana Chalukyan Pierced Stone Lattice Windows (Siddhesvara)
cuisine: Byadgi Chilli-Spiced Jolada Rotti & Ennegayi (Byadgi Chilli GI No. 129)
traditions: Devaragudda Karanika (Annual Prophetic Oracle Custom)
Syncretic Hindu–Sufi Literary Legacy of Shishunala Sharif
heritageSites: Kaginele Kanakadasa Heritage Complex & Shishunala Tomb

name: Kalaburagi
monumentDescription: 14th-century Bahmani stone fortress housing 15 watchtowers, a rare fully roofed 63-dome Jama Masjid (1367 CE), and the 29-foot Bara Gazi cannon.
culturalSignificance: First capital of the Bahmani Sultanate (1347–1424 CE), preserving Malkhed's 9th-century Rashtrakuta imperial heritage, Sannati Mauryan-Satavahana excavations, and Khwaja Bande Nawaz Sufi shrine.
description: Historic Kalyana Karnataka center bridging Manyakheta (Malkhed) Rashtrakuta rule, Sannati's Mauryan-Satavahana Buddhist stupa, and the founding Bahmani Sultanate citadel.
history: Kalaburagi's heritage stretches back to Manyakheta (Malkhed), capital of the Rashtrakuta Empire (8th–10th century CE) and birthplace of Kannada poetics ('Kavirajamarga'), as well as Kanaganahalli near Sannati where an inscribed relief of Emperor Ashoka was unearthed. In 1347 CE, Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah established Kalaburagi as the first Bahmani capital.
arts: Early Bahmani Vaulted Stone & Mortar Architecture
cuisine: Kalaburagi Tur Dal (GI App. No. 570) & Jolada Rotti
traditions: Syncretic Sufi & Veerashaiva Sharanaru Pilgrimage Traditions
Kavirajamarga Classical Kannada Literary Heritage
heritageSites: Haft Gumbaz & Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah

name: Kodagu
monumentDescription: 17th-century hilltop citadel built in mud by Muddu Raja and rebuilt in granite under Tipu Sultan and Lingarajendra Wadiyar II, enclosing a museum and clock tower.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Kodagu's highland history alongside Talakaveri (source of the Kaveri River), community-guarded Devarakadu sacred groves, Bylakuppe Tibetan monasteries, and Kodava warrior traditions.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology & Forest Department
description: Highland Western Ghats district celebrated for Talakaveri—headwaters of the Kaveri—ancestral Devarakadu sacred forest groves, Kodava festivals, and Madikeri Fort.
history: Ruled by the Haleri kings from the 17th to 19th centuries CE, Kodagu preserved distinct mountain martial and agricultural customs. Its landscapes safeguard over 1,200 community-protected Devarakadu sacred groves alongside the sacred spring of Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills.
festivals: Tula Sankramana (Kaveri Sankramana at Talakaveri, October)
traditions: Devarakadu Sacred Forest Grove Community Stewardship
Ainmane Ancestral Kodava Joint-Family Houses

name: Kolar
monumentDescription: 11th-century Chola-patronized Kolaramma granite temple complex bearing Tamil and Kannada inscriptions beside the ornate Vijayanagara-period Someshwara temple and kalyani tank.
culturalSignificance: Preserves rare Western Ganga, Chola, and Vijayanagara epigraphs from Kuvalalapura alongside Avani's Ramalingeshwara group and Bangaru Tirupati.
description: Ancient Eastern Maidan district known as Kuvalalapura under the Western Gangas, preserving Chola-period granite temples at Kolar and Avani alongside centuries-old tank systems.
history: Kolar served as an early capital of the Western Ganga dynasty (4th–10th century CE) before becoming a stronghold of Chola rulers who rebuilt Kolaramma Temple in the 11th century, followed by Vijayanagara mandapas at Someshwara and Kurudumale.
arts: Chola & Western Ganga Granite Epigraphy and Reliefs
cuisine: Ragi Mudde with Avarekalu & Horse Gram Bassaru
traditions: Inscribed Scorpion & Votive Offerings at Kolaramma
Ancient Interconnected Kolar Kere Tank Irrigation

name: Koppal
monumentDescription: 1112 CE Kalyana Chalukyan soapstone sanctuary lauded in contemporary epigraphs as 'Devalaya Chakravarti' (Emperor among Temples), featuring a 68-pillar open mandapa.
culturalSignificance: Monumental zenith of 12th-century Chalukyan architecture alongside Ashokan rock edicts at Koppal, Anegundi across the Tungabhadra from Hampi, and GI-certified Kinhal Craft.
description: Tungabhadra–Anegundi heartland preserving Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts, the 1112 CE Mahadeva Temple at Itagi, Navalinga temples at Kuknur, and GI-certified Kinhal painted wooden craft.
history: Koppal carries inscriptions spanning Ashoka Maurya (Gavimath & Palkigundu), the Rashtrakutas (Kuknur Navalinga), Kalyana Chalukyas (Itagi), and early Vijayanagara (Anegundi). Its Chitragara artisan families in Kinhal have practiced lightweight polki-wood carving and natural lacquer painting since Vijayanagara times.
arts: Kinhal (Kinnal) Craft Painted Woodwork (GI App. No. 212, 2011)
traditions: Kinhal Chitragara Family Wood & Tamarind-Seed Paste Craft
Gavisiddheshwara Community Anna Dasoha Tradition

name: Mandya
monumentDescription: 1784 CE teakwood garden palace adorned with vivid battle and court murals within the historic Kaveri river island fortress of Srirangapatna.
culturalSignificance: Unites 9th-century Sri Ranganathaswamy temple heritage, Ramanujacharya's Melukote philosophical center, Hoysala temples at Hosaholalu and Kikkeri, and 18th-century Mysore murals.
description: Fertile Kaveri basin district anchored by the historic island capital of Srirangapatna, Melukote's Cheluvanarayana temple and Sanskrit academy, and ornate Hoysala shrines.
history: Srirangapatna served as a key Vijayanagara viceroyalty and later royal capital of the Kingdom of Mysore under the Wadiyars, Hyder Ali, and Tipu Sultan prior to 1799 CE. Nearby Melukote (Thirunarayanapuram) became a premier center of Vishishtadvaita philosophy in the 12th century under Acharya Ramanuja.
festivals: Kaveri Cauvery River Worship & Makara Sankranthi
arts: Daria Daulat Wall Murals & Indo-Islamic Woodwork
cuisine: Ragi Mudde with Nati-style or Veg Saaru
Mandya Jaggery (Organic Sugarcane Bella) & Maddur Vada

Kaveri River Basin Paddy & Sugarcane Agrarian Heritage

name: Mysuru
monumentDescription: Indo-Saracenic royal residence rebuilt between 1897 and 1912 CE under the Wadiyar dynasty, blending Rajput domes, stained glass, and carved rosewood halls.
culturalSignificance: Focal stage for Karnataka's Nada Habba Mysuru Dasara, UNESCO-listed Keshava Temple at Somnathapura, Mysore Traditional Paintings (GI No. 32), and KSIC Mysore Silk (GI No. 22).
monumentAttribution: Mysore Palace Board & Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC)
description: Cultural capital of southern Karnataka, anchored by Amba Vilas Palace, UNESCO-listed Keshava Temple at Somnathapura, Bylakuppe's Namdroling Monastery, Nada Habba Mysuru Dasara, and GI crafts.
history: Ruled by the Wadiyar dynasty from 1399 CE (and restored after 1799 CE under Krishnaraja Wadiyar III and IV), Mysuru nurtured Indo-Saracenic civic architecture, Carnatic music, gold-gilded gesso painting, pure mulberry silk weaving, and Nanjangud-Somnathapura temple traditions.
festivals: Mysuru Dasara & Jambu Savari (Official Nada Habba)
Losar Celebrations at Bylakuppe Tibetan Settlement
arts: Mysore Rosewood Inlay Craft (GI App. No. 54, 2007)
Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase & Kamsale Processional Folk Arts
cuisine: Mysore Pak (Gram Flour, Sugar & Pure Ghee Confection)
traditions: KSIC Mysore Silk Pure Zari Weaving (GI App. No. 22, 2005)
Wadiyar Court Music & Chamundi Hill Stone-Step Pilgrimage

name: Raichur
monumentDescription: 1294 CE Kakatiya-built hill fortress erected by Gore Gangaya Reddivaru, notable for its cyclopean dry-stone ramparts, Sikandar Gate, and 12-meter inscribed monolith.
culturalSignificance: Key strategic monument of the Krishna–Tungabhadra Raichur Doab alongside Maski's 1915 Ashokan inscription—the first edict found bearing Ashoka's personal name.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Historic Krishna–Tungabhadra Doab district renowned for Raichur Fort, Maski's Ashokan inscription, Mudgal Fort, and the Haridasa devotional music of Vijayadasa and Jagannathadasa.
history: In 1915, C. Beadon discovered the Maski Minor Rock Edict here—the very first Ashokan inscription explicitly naming 'Devanampriya Ashoka'. Later, the fertile Doab saw fiercely contested rule between Kakatiyas, Bahmanis, Adil Shahis, and the Vijayanagara Empire, while Manvi and Lingasugur shaped Karnataka's Dasa Sahitya movement.
cuisine: Jolada Rotti, Sajje Rotti & Shengadani Chutney
traditions: Dasa Sahitya Bhajana & Tamboori Oral Tradition
Krishna–Tungabhadra Doab Tank Irrigation Heritage

name: Ramanagara
monumentDescription: Granite monolith range crowned by medieval stone temples above the Arkavathi valley, overlooking Channapatna's artisan craft corridor and Janapada Loka folk museum.
culturalSignificance: Unites Channapatna Wooden Toys & Dolls (GI No. 23), Karnataka's premier Janapada Loka folk arts museum, and Magadi Kempegowda heritage.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC) & IP India GI Registry
description: Home to Channapatna ('Gombegala Ooru'), internationally recognized for botanical lac-finished wooden toys (GI No. 23), Janapada Loka folk arts campus, and Kempegowda's Magadi forts.
history: Channapatna's lacquerware craft received royal encouragement in the late 18th century under Tipu Sultan, who invited Persian artisans to train local woodworkers using seasoned Aale Mara (Wrightia tinctoria). Meanwhile, Magadi and Savandurga preserve fortifications of Bengaluru founder Kempe Gowda's descendants, and Ramanagara hosts the Janapada Loka folk museum founded by H.L. Nage Gowda.
festivals: Janapada Loka Lokotsava (Annual Folk Arts Festival)
arts: Channapatna Wooden Toys & Dolls (GI App. No. 23, 2006)
Janapada Loka Folk Instrument & Puppet Archive
Ramanagara Silk Cocoon Reeling & Filature Heritage

traditions: Zero-Toxic Botanical Lac & Ivory-Wood Turning Guilds
H.L. Nage Gowda Folk Preservation Stewardship

name: Shivamogga
monumentDescription: 16th-century granite sanctuary built by the Keladi Nayakas, uniting Vijayanagara mandapas with coastal sloping eaves and a sculpted Nandi pavilion.
culturalSignificance: Testament to the Keladi Nayaka kingdom alongside Keladi Rameshwara Temple, Balligavi's Kalyana Chalukyan shrines, Kudali, and Heggodu's Ninasam theatre.
description: Malnad cultural powerhouse spanning the Keladi Nayaka monuments at Ikkeri and Kavaledurga, Chalukyan Balligavi (birthplace of Allama Prabhu), Kuppali (Kuvempu's home), and Ninasam at Heggodu.
history: Ruled successively by Kadambas, Chalukyas, Hoysalas, and the Keladi Nayakas (notably Shivappa Nayaka and Rani Chennamma of Keladi), Shivamogga preserves medieval Balligavi (ancient Balipura), Keladi, and Ikkeri. In modern Karnataka, Kuppali nurtured Jnanpith laureate Rashtrakavi Kuvempu while Heggodu's Ninasam became a landmark of rural theatre and Yakshagana dialogue.
arts: Chittara Folk Wall & Threshold Painting (Sagara Women's Art)
cuisine: Malnad Akki Rotti, Halasina (Jackfruit) Kadubu & Thambuli
traditions: Chittara Rice-Paste Geometric Threshold Art
Hase & Malnad Monsoon Forest Festival Customs

name: Tumakuru
monumentDescription: 17th-century hilltop fortification rising up Asia's second-largest monolithic rock dome, engineered with multi-gate stone ramparts, granaries, and steep rock-cut steps.
culturalSignificance: Dramatic fusion of Deccan hill-fort masonry alongside Nolamba-period Bhoganandishwara/Kalleshwara temples at Aralaguppe, Siddaganga heritage, and Devarayanadurga.
description: Plains and monolith hill-fort district crowned by Madhugiri Fort, Devarayanadurga, 9th-century Nolamba and 13th-century Hoysala temples at Aralaguppe, and Pavagada Fort.
history: Tumakuru features important 9th–10th century Nolamba Pallava temples at Hemavati (Sira border) and Aralaguppe, the Hoysala Channakeshava temple at Aralaguppe, and fortified monoliths at Madhugiri and Midigeshi built by local Gowda chieftains and strengthened under Hyder Ali.
cuisine: Ragi Mudde with Avarekalu Saaru & Bassaru
Tumakuru Tatte Idli & Pavagada Groundnut Snacks

Sira & Madhugiri Hilltop Rainwater Cistern Engineering

name: Udupi
monumentDescription: 13th-century coastal monastery complex founded by Madhvacharya featuring tiled coastal roofs, the Madhwa Sarovara tank, and the carved Kanakana Kindi viewing window.
culturalSignificance: Center of Dvaita Vedanta philosophy, the biennial Paryaya festival, Badaguthittu Yakshagana theatre, Udupi cotton sarees (GI No. 103), and Udupi vegetarian temple cuisine.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC) & Sangeet Natak Akademi
description: Coastal cultural and culinary hub celebrated for Sri Krishna Matha and biennial Paryaya, Badaguthittu Yakshagana theatre, Barkur's medieval ruins, Udupi handloom sarees, and vegetarian Udupi cuisine.
history: Founded in the 13th century CE by philosopher-saint Madhvacharya, Udupi evolved around the Ashta Mathas rotating stewardship every two years (Paryaya). Neighboring Barkur (Barakanur) served as an ancient Tuluva coastal capital under the Alupas and Vijayanagara governors.

All-Night Yakshagana Prasanga Palm-Leaf Preservation

name: Uttara Kannada
monumentDescription: Coastal sanctuary perched on Kanduka headland surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea, crowned by its monumental 20-storey Raja Gopura.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Uttara Kannada's coastal-ghat continuum alongside Banavasi (Karnataka's first Kadamba royal capital), Gokarna Mahabaleshwar, and Mirjan laterite fort.
description: Coastal and Sahyadri rainforest district bridging Banavasi (4th-century capital of Karnataka's Kadamba dynasty), Gokarna's Mahabaleshwar shrine, Mirjan Fort, and Kanduka coastal headlands.
history: Banavasi on the Varada river served as the capital of Karnataka's earliest indigenous imperial dynasty—the Kadambas founded by Mayurasharma around 345 CE—and was celebrated by Kannada poet Adikavi Pampa. Along the Konkan-Karwar coast, Mirjan Fort and Gokarna became key maritime and pilgrimage crossroads.

name: Vijayanagara
geoBoundaryNote: Carved out of Ballari on November 17, 2021; represented within the Ballari boundary polygon in the 2021 geoBoundaries LGD snapshot.
monumentDescription: 15th–16th century Vijayanagara granite masterpiece housing the iconic interlocking Stone Chariot and slender monolithic mandapa colonnades along the Tungabhadra River.
culturalSignificance: Heart of the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments at Hampi (Ref. 241, 1986), exemplifying medieval Deccan imperial urbanism, hydrology, and stonecraft.
description: Karnataka's 31st district, encompassing the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments at Hampi along the Tungabhadra River and the Mailara folk traditions of Hadagali.
history: Founded in 1336 CE by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I and reaching its zenith under Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE), Hampi was one of the world's largest cities in the early 16th century. Formed as a separate district headquartered at Hosapete in November 2021, Vijayanagara also preserves Kalyana Chalukyan shrines at Kuruvatti and Bagali-border traditions.

Purandaradasa Carnatic Music Heritage (Pitamaha of Carnatic Music)

name: Vijayapura
monumentDescription: 17th-century Adil Shahi mausoleum completed in 1656 CE for Mohammed Adil Shah, crowned by a monumental unsupported masonry dome and acoustic Whispering Gallery.
culturalSignificance: Pinnacle of Deccan Indo-Islamic structural engineering alongside Ibrahim Rauza, Bara Kaman, and ancient Kudala Sangama—resting place of 12th-century reformer Basavanna.
description: Deccan architectural capital of the Adil Shahi dynasty, centered around Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza, and home to Kudala Sangama at the Krishna–Malaprabha confluence.
history: Vijayapura (formerly Bijapur) flourished as the capital of the Adil Shahi Sultanate (1490–1686 CE), producing architectural breakthroughs such as Gol Gumbaz's intersecting pendentive dome, Ibrahim Rauza, and gravity-fed terracotta waterworks (Taj Bawdi). Along its southern river boundary, Kudala Sangama is revered as the samadhi site of 12th-century poet-philosopher Basavanna.
arts: Adil Shahi Intersecting-Arch Masonry & Stucco Work
cuisine: Jolada Rotti, Sajje Rotti & Khadak Rotti
traditions: Historic Karez & Bawdi Stepwell Urban Water Network
Lingayat Vachana & Sharana Pilgrimage at Kudala Sangama

name: Yadgir
monumentDescription: Hilltop fortress perched on a dramatic granite monolith overlooking the Bhima valley, preserving Yadavas of Devagiri, Bahmani, and Adil Shahi masonry, gateways, and rock water tanks.
culturalSignificance: Marks the Bhima–Krishna riverine corridor connecting Yadgir Fort, Shorapur (Surpur) Bedar Nayaka heritage, and the natural 'Sleeping Buddha' granite formation near Shahpur.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Bhima–Krishna river basin district formed in 2010, home to the Yadava-Bahmani Yadgir Fort, Surpur Bedar Nayaka heritage (Venkatappa Nayaka), and Shahpur's granite hills.
history: Known historically as Yetagiri under the Yadavas of Devagiri, Yadgir passed through Bahmani and Adil Shahi hands before becoming part of the Nizam's Dominions. Its Shorapur (Surpur) principality was ruled by the Bedar Nayakas—remembered for Raja Venkatappa Nayaka's resistance in the 1857 uprising and Taylor's Manzil heritage residence.
